Relying on universal systems for equitable care is a fantasy when rationing hits the most vulnerable hardest, while private markets, with targeted subsidies, deliver faster, better solutions to those in need.
Universal systems, even with ample funding, often collapse under bureaucratic weight, delivering neither equity nor efficiency compared to the sharp, results-driven focus of private healthcare.

Targeted subsidies for the most vulnerable ensure that support is pinpointed directly to those who need it most, unlike a universal system that often wastes resources on those who can fend for themselves.
